title: Candidate DAG Verification under Unknown Off-Target Intervention Laws
banked_reason: The proposed fallback to a common approximation comparator names neither that comparator nor the formal risk-and-certificate relation; at K=1 and delta=0 the stated polynomial sandwich forces exact weighted set-cover optimization unless P=NP.
gap_reasons: The proposed fallback to a ‘common approximation comparator’ names neither that comparator nor the formal risk-and-certificate relation, so it cannot presently replace the exact-oracle claim or support the field-tier promised advance.

For K=1 and deterministic product laws encoding set cover, the required sandwich includes r=0; with delta=0 it forces an inner controller of zero excess and hence exact known-law optimization, contradicting the requested polynomial constructor unless P=NP.

The final conditional alternative invokes an explicitly defined common approximation comparator, but no comparator object, value function, excess region, or dual relation for it is defined in the core.
proof_attempt_summary: Four proposal versions attempted to define a stopped one-shot excess-cost frontier relative to the exact known-law adaptive covering oracle, with a polynomial controller and information-theoretic inner/outer certificates. The central contract collapses on deterministic K=1 instances: zero excess at delta=0 requires exact weighted-set-cover optimization, while the fallback approximation comparator was never defined. A sound conditional hardness proposition and supporting stopped Bellman/KL machinery remain, but a field-tier continuation must begin as a new comparator-relative research pivot.
tldr: For a candidate DAG explicitly supplied to a verifier, can one characterize the one-shot price of not knowing which member of a finite rational product-Bernoulli off-target-law table governs the episode, using only public information observed before verification finishes? The proposed field-tier contribution is a non-oracular, checkable coordinatewise inner/outer approximation to the excess-cost region, based on certified finite-state controllers and common-policy full-target realization-plan duals. Exact one-edge, fork, and shared-law two-fork calculations are a mandatory kill test before any general theorem.
gap: The causal anchor gives known-law candidate verification and a qualitative unknown-law obstruction. Neighboring cover, bandit, and stochastic-shortest-path theories either know the law, learn across repeated tasks, impose growing-horizon discrimination, or do not provide a common-policy polyhedral certificate for one absorbing episode.
fill: First solve exact rational minimax and certificate problems on three diagnostic families. Then determine whether polynomially many certified controllers and finite-horizon realization-plan dual cuts give a coordinatewise multiplicative-additive sandwich of the attainable excess region under the declared bit model.
